key_takeaways: Current health expenditure was 10.74 percent of GDP in 2023, down from a peak of 12.32 percent in 2022.{{health_system.financing:1}}
People aged 65 and over are 29.4 percent of the population, projected to reach 38.7 percent by 2070.{{country_overview.demographics:1}}{{health_system.outlook:2}}
General hospitals averaged a profit margin of minus 7.3 percent in fiscal 2024, and public hospitals minus 18.5 percent.{{health_system.private_system:2}}
Fees rise 3.09 percent on average over fiscal 2026 and 2027, the first net increase in 12 years.{{health_system.outlook:4}}{{health_system.outlook:5}}
health_system: Statutory health insurance is universal, and enrollment in an employment-based or residence-based plan is required.{{health_system.public_system:1}}
Patients usually pay 30 percent of costs, while people aged 75 and over pay 10 percent.{{health_system.public_system:2}}
Japan had 347,772 registered physicians at the end of 2024, or 280.9 per 100,000 people.{{health_system.workforce:1}}
market: Medical corporations ran 5,550 of 7,941 hospitals in August 2026; public bodies ran about 15 percent.{{health_system.private_system:1}}
The tracker lists 66 active partnerships with 64 foreign institutions, 19 of them US centers.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:1}}
Hospitals accredited by Medical Excellence JAPAN admitted 2,099 new international patients in fiscal 2024.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:5}}
risks: Births hit a record low of 671,270 in 2025, and the population is projected to fall to 87 million.{{country_overview.demographics:6}}{{country_overview.demographics:10}}
The Finance Ministry expects a doctor surplus after 2032 and urges a planned cut in medical school enrollment.{{health_system.outlook:7}}
Real GDP edged down less than 0.1 percent in July to September 2026, the first decline in four quarters.{{country_overview.economy:5}}

recent.text: Ministers agreed on 24 December 2025 to raise main fees 3.09 percent on average over fiscal 2026 and 2027.{{recent_developments.4:1}}
The health ministry reported fiscal 2024 national medical expenditure of ¥48.81 trillion (US$311 billion), up 1.5 percent.{{recent_developments.1:1}}
Medical Excellence JAPAN launched an official portal for international patients on 12 November 2026.{{recent_developments.0:1}}

country_background: Japan, a parliamentary constitutional monarchy with its capital in Tokyo, counted 122.97 million residents in the 2025 census.{{country_overview.demographics:3}}{{country_overview.demographics:8}}{{country_overview.demographics:1}} The Emperor is the symbol of the State, and Sanae Takaichi of the Liberal Democratic Party became prime minister in October 2025 and was designated again in February 2026.{{country_overview.government:1}}{{country_overview.government:3}}{{country_overview.government:4}} The economy was about 7.03 trillion international dollars at purchasing power parity in 2025, fifth largest in the world.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:2}} Life expectancy was 81.35 years for men and 87.33 for women in 2025, and 29.4 percent of people were 65 or older.{{country_overview.demographics:7}}{{country_overview.demographics:1}} The key risk is demographic: births hit a record low in 2025, and the population is projected to fall to 87 million by 2070.{{country_overview.demographics:6}}{{country_overview.demographics:10}}
